questiontext.text:
Consider this list of decimals:


{@floatList@}


Answer the following without a calculator:


(a) Write this same list of decimals rounded to one decimal place.

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

(1)

[[feedback:prt1]]


(b) Add the largest and the smallest numbers from the list together.

Give your answer exactly

[[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]]

(1)

[[feedback:prt2]]


(c) Subtract the fourth largest decimal from the third largest.

Give your answer exactly

[[input:ans3]] [[validation:ans3]]

(1)

[[feedback:prt3]]


(d) Write down two decimals from the list which when divided will give a whole number, and what is the whole number?

[[input:ans4]] \(\div\) [[input:ans5]] \(=\) [[input:ans6]] [[validation:ans4]] [[validation:ans5]] [[validation:ans6]]

(1)

[[feedback:prt4]]


(e) Write two decimals from the list when added together will give a whole number, and what is the whole number?

[[input:ans7]] \(+\) [[input:ans8]] \(=\) [[input:ans9]] [[validation:ans7]] [[validation:ans8]] [[validation:ans9]]

(1)

[[feedback:prt5]]


(f) Which two numbers when multiplied together give you a number closest to 0?

You do not need to calculate the product

[[input:ans10]] and [[input:ans11]] [[validation:ans10]] [[validation:ans11]]

(1)

[[feedback:prt6]]
